model_note.S:
cc: Food sticking and unintentional weight loss

HPI: 26 yo m. Patient reports: It began 8 weeks ago. Food seems to stop behind my breastbone. There is no pain spreading to the arms or back. It feels like food sticks after I swallow. I have lost 10 pounds without trying. Solid food was the problem first; now soft foods are becoming difficult. I have had years of heartburn. Small bites and water sometimes help food pass. Meat and bread are hardest to swallow. Over-the-counter antacid helps heartburn but not the sticking. This progressive sticking is new. Solid food sticks after swallowing. Sometimes food comes back up. I lost 10 pounds in 2 months. I have less energy.

Patient perspective: My father had cancer. Is that what this is?

PMH: Longstanding reflux; no prior endoscopy.

PSH: No surgeries or admissions.

Meds: Calcium carbonate antacid as needed. Hydrocortisone 1% cream to eczema patches once daily for up to 1 week during flares.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One alcoholic drink weekly. No recreational drugs. Bicycle mechanic; lives with wife; still able to swallow liquids and manage saliva.

FH: My mother is still alive, and she had a stroke when she was seventy-eight.; My father died of lung cancer when he was seventy.; I have one sister and she is healthy.

ROS: Gastrointestinal - Reports dysphagia. Denies odynophagia. Reports regurgitation. General - Reports weight loss. Reports fatigue. Denies fever. Respiratory - Denies cough. Denies dyspnea. Denies hemoptysis.
Additional PMH: I have had eczema since childhood.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.1 F oral, P 82 bpm, BP 124/76 mmHg, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Thin appearing; handles secretions without distress.

Heart: Regular rhythm without murmur.

Lungs: Clear breath sounds bilaterally.

HEENT: Oropharynx without visible lesions. No palpable cervical or supraclavicular nodes.

Abd: Abdomen not distended. Bowel sounds present. No focal tenderness with gentle palpation. Tympanic in examined quadrants.

Osteopathic: T5 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Arrange expedited gastroenterology assessment and upper endoscopy with esophageal biopsies; review hydration and nutrition and consider clinician-directed acid suppression without delaying investigation; explain structural and inflammatory possibilities; follow up within 1 week to confirm referral progress, with immediate emergency care if unable to swallow liquids or saliva.

2. Review reflux history and obtain upper endoscopy to assess a possible esophageal stricture; discuss clinician-directed acid suppression while specialist investigation proceeds; explain safe food textures and the need for urgent care if food lodges or liquids cannot pass.

3. Explain that cancer is less likely at this age but progressive dysphagia and weight loss require investigation; use endoscopy/biopsy and specialist referral as indicated; agree on a contact plan while awaiting results rather than reassurance based only on age.

model_note.S:
cc: Food sticking and unintentional weight loss

HPI: 26 yo m. Patient reports: It began 5 weeks ago. Food seems to stop behind my breastbone. There is no pain spreading to the arms or back. It feels like food sticks after I swallow. I have lost 10 pounds without trying. Solid food was the problem first; now soft foods are becoming difficult. I have had years of heartburn. Small bites and water sometimes help food pass. Meat and bread are hardest to swallow. Over-the-counter antacid helps heartburn but not the sticking. This progressive sticking is new. Solid food sticks after swallowing. Sometimes food comes back up. I lost 10 pounds in 2 months. I have less energy.

Patient perspective: My father had cancer. Is that what this is?

PMH: Longstanding reflux; no prior endoscopy.

PSH: No surgeries or admissions.

Meds: Calcium carbonate antacid as needed. Hydrocortisone 1% cream to eczema patches once daily for up to 1 week during flares.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One alcoholic drink weekly. No recreational drugs. Bicycle mechanic; lives with wife; still able to swallow liquids and manage saliva.

FH: My mother is still alive, and she had a stroke when she was seventy-eight.; My father died of lung cancer when he was seventy.; I have one sister and she is healthy.

ROS: Gastrointestinal - Reports dysphagia. Denies odynophagia. Reports regurgitation. General - Reports weight loss. Reports fatigue. Denies fever. Respiratory - Denies cough. Denies dyspnea. Denies hemoptysis.
Additional PMH: I have had eczema since childhood.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 98.1 F oral, P 82 bpm, BP 124/76 mmHg, R 16 rpm, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Thin appearing; handles secretions without distress.

Heart: Regular rhythm without murmur.

Lungs: Clear breath sounds bilaterally.

HEENT: Oropharynx without visible lesions. No palpable cervical or supraclavicular nodes.

Abd: Abdomen not distended. Bowel sounds present. No focal tenderness with gentle palpation. Tympanic in examined quadrants.

Osteopathic: T5 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Arrange expedited gastroenterology assessment and upper endoscopy with esophageal biopsies; review hydration and nutrition and consider clinician-directed acid suppression without delaying investigation; explain structural and inflammatory possibilities; follow up within 1 week to confirm referral progress, with immediate emergency care if unable to swallow liquids or saliva.

2. Review reflux history and obtain upper endoscopy to assess a possible esophageal stricture; discuss clinician-directed acid suppression while specialist investigation proceeds; explain safe food textures and the need for urgent care if food lodges or liquids cannot pass.

3. Explain that cancer is less likely at this age but progressive dysphagia and weight loss require investigation; use endoscopy/biopsy and specialist referral as indicated; agree on a contact plan while awaiting results rather than reassurance based only on age.
